Subject: language
Name: Language name
Description: The name a registry gives this language. Registries disagree; every name is kept and attributed rather than one winning.

Subject: language
Name: Alternate name
Description: An additional name a registry records for this language.

Subject: language
Name: ISO 639-1 code
Description: Two-letter code, where one exists.

Subject: language
Name: ISO scope
Description: Individual, Macrolanguage or Special, as ISO 639-3 classifies it.

Subject: language
Name: ISO language type
Description: Living, Extinct, Ancient, Historical or Constructed, per ISO 639-3.

Subject: language
Name: Macrolanguage
Description: The macrolanguage this individual language belongs to.

Subject: language
Name: Macrolanguage member
Description: An individual language belonging to this macrolanguage.

Subject: language
Name: Glottocode
Description: Glottolog's identifier for this languoid.

Subject: language
Name: Modality
Description: Signed or spoken, derived by walking Glottolog's parent edges to the root and testing it against the Sign Language pseudo-family (sign1238). Glottolog never states a modality; the walk and the reading are ours. Replaces a heuristic that matched ISO Ref_Name against /sign language/i plus a hand-written allowlist of four endonymous codes, and which missed 64 sign languages.

Subject: language
Name: Glottolog bucket
Description: The top-level Glottolog bucket a language sits in when that bucket classifies by KIND rather than descent -- Unclassifiable, Unattested, Artificial Language, Speech Register, Pidgin, Mixed Language. Kept as its own field because putting it in the family slot would assert a genealogical descent Glottolog never claimed. A card with this field has no family, and that is the honest result.

Subject: language
Name: Is isolate
Description: Whether Glottolog classifies this as a language isolate.

Subject: language
Name: Family
Description: The top-level family a classification authority places this language in. Glottolog and WALS are separate taxonomies that do not always agree — WALS puts Plains Cree in Algic with genus Algonquian, Glottolog in algi1248 — so both are kept and attributed. The Glottolog value must match the cited glottocode (lint R5).

Subject: language
Name: Family glottocode
Description: Glottocode of the top-level family.

Subject: language
Name: Genus
Description: WALS's intermediate classification node. This is a WALS concept, NOT a Glottolog one — Glottolog publishes an arbitrary-depth tree with no genus level, so sourcing it from Glottolog was a category error. The Glottolog hierarchy is carried by `ancestry` instead.

Subject: language
Name: Ancestry
Description: An ancestor glottocode on the path from family to this languoid, in order.

Subject: language
Name: Dialect count
Description: Direct child dialects, as Glottolog's own child_dialect_count column states it. This is GLOTTOLOG'S assertion, not our arithmetic — an earlier registry claimed it as champollion-derived, which took credit for someone else's count. Direct children only, not the whole subtree.

Subject: language
Name: Latitude
Description: Representative point, as Glottolog gives it. Not a territory.

Subject: language
Name: Longitude
Description: Representative point, as Glottolog gives it. Not a territory.

Subject: language
Name: Macroarea
Description: Glottolog's macroarea.

Subject: language
Name: Country
Description: A country Glottolog associates with this language.

Subject: language
Name: Speaker count
Description: What a body states about speaker numbers, VERBATIM. Not an integer: ELCat publishes BANDS — 1-9, 10-99, 100-999, 1000-9999, 10000-99999 — and the word Awakening, and only one of its seven forms is a plain number. Coercing a band to a midpoint would manufacture a precision no source claims. Estimates disagree and are date-dependent; all are kept and attributed.

Subject: language
Name: Endangerment
Description: An assessing body's vitality judgement, in that body's own words. The bodies use different scales — ELCat has nine levels including awakening and dormant, Glottolog AES has six — so each scale is declared in codes.csv against its own Source_Scale and a vocabulary difference is never rendered as a disagreement.

Subject: language
Name: Consonant count
Description: OURS: a COUNT over the segments of a cited PHOIBLE inventory, where SegmentClass is consonant. PHOIBLE publishes one row per segment and asserts no count, so this is a Champollion derivation and must not wear PHOIBLE's name. Marginal segments ARE included, as PHOIBLE's own published counts do.

Subject: language
Name: Vowel count
Description: OURS: a COUNT over the segments of a cited PHOIBLE inventory where SegmentClass is vowel. Marginal segments included.

Subject: language
Name: Tone count
Description: OURS: a COUNT over the segments of a cited PHOIBLE inventory where SegmentClass is tone. PHOIBLE is the sole tone authority (lint R1) — Grambank has no tone feature at all, and WALS chapter 13A is a different question.

Subject: language
Name: Has tone
Description: Whether the PHOIBLE inventory records any tone.

Subject: language
Name: Total phonemes
Description: OURS: consonants + vowels + tones from the cited PHOIBLE inventory.

Subject: language
Name: Word order
Description: Dominant order of subject, object and verb.

Subject: language
Name: Subject-verb order
Description: Order of subject and verb.

Subject: language
Name: Fusion
Description: Degree of fusion of selected inflectional formatives.

Subject: language
Name: Verb synthesis
Description: Number of categories per word in the verb.

Subject: language
Name: Affix preference
Description: Prefixing versus suffixing in inflectional morphology.

Subject: language
Name: Reduplication
Description: Presence and productivity of reduplication.

Subject: language
Name: Gender count
Description: Number of grammatical genders.

Subject: language
Name: Case count
Description: Number of morphological cases.

Subject: language
Name: Verbal alignment
Description: Alignment of verbal person marking.

Subject: language
Name: Negation order
Description: Order of negative morpheme and verb.

Subject: language
Name: Has numeral classifiers
Description: Whether the language uses numeral classifiers.

Subject: language
Name: Has gender in pronouns
Description: Whether independent pronouns mark gender.

Subject: language
Name: Has core case
Description: Whether core arguments carry case marking.

Subject: language
Name: Has oblique case
Description: Whether oblique arguments carry case marking.

Subject: language
Name: Marks past tense
Description: Whether past tense is morphologically marked.

Subject: language
Name: Marks present tense
Description: Whether present tense is morphologically marked.

Subject: language
Name: Has sex-based gender
Description: Whether the gender system is sex-based.

Subject: language
Name: MED level
Description: Glottolog's Most Extensive Description level: grammar, grammar sketch, phonology, wordlist and so on.

Subject: language
Name: MED source ID
Description: Bibliographic key of the most extensive description.

Subject: language
Name: First documented
Description: The earliest year of documentation Glottolog records. GLOTTOLOG'S column (First_Year_Of_Documentation), not our arithmetic -- present on only 217 languages, which is itself worth knowing.

Subject: language
Name: Last documented
Description: The most recent year of documentation Glottolog records. GLOTTOLOG'S column (Last_Year_Of_Documentation), present on 1,076 languages.

Subject: language
Name: Endonym
Description: The name speakers use for their own language. ATTRIBUTED across LinguaMeta and Wikidata P1705, because a language may have several native names in several scripts and communities do not always agree which is right -- choosing a primary one would be this project making a call that is not its to make. `nativeName` was a SECOND field for this same concept sourced from Wikidata; merging them is the one-concept-one-field rule applied to my own registry.

Subject: language
Name: BCP 47 tag
Description: IETF language tag.

Subject: language
Name: CLDR official status
Description: Official status CLDR records for this language in some territory.

Subject: language
Name: Script
Description: An ISO 15924 script code used to write this language.

Subject: language
Name: Script name
Description: OURS: the ISO 15924 registry name for a script code another source recorded. A LIST, because a language can use several -- Plains Cree is written in both Unified Canadian Aboriginal Syllabics and Latin, and projecting a single value silently dropped one. Unicode says what a code means; it says nothing about which languages use it, so the composite is champollion-derived.

Subject: language
Name: Text direction
Description: Writing direction, from CLDR.

Subject: language
Name: Numeral base
Description: The numeral base, VERBATIM from Chan's Base column. 2,777 of 5,332 languages (52%) have it EMPTY and empty means empty -- a previous generator assigned a base anyway and invented 2,005 values. Chan records 94 distinct bases including binary, body tally, quinary-vigesimal and complicated; flattening those to decimal destroyed exactly the systems that change an MT pipeline.

Subject: language
Name: Highest numeral elicited
Description: The highest numeral the questionnaire elicited. A fact about the questionnaire, not about the language's counting.

Subject: language
Name: Colexification concepts
Description: OURS: count of CLICS concepts attested for this language.

Subject: language
Name: Colexifying forms
Description: OURS: forms in this language that map to TWO OR MORE distinct Concepticon concepts in CLICS3 -- the colexifications. Bounded by colexificationConcepts and checked against it: the previous corpus shipped cards where this exceeded the concept count, which is arithmetically impossible and means the join was wrong.

Subject: language
Name: Lexical resource
Description: A published wordlist covering this language, with its concept count. Existence and coverage only — never a typological claim. Variant names the dataset.

Subject: language
Name: Dictionary resource
Description: A published dictionary covering this language. EXISTENCE, never quality: that somebody publishes one, never that it is good, complete, or usable. Two upstreams write here and they carry different detail — a CLDF dictionary dataset knows its entry count, a GiellaLT/ALTLab repository knows the pair and direction — so entries are not uniform in shape, and each says which source it came from. They are ONE parameter because they are one fact; forking a second would make has a dictionary mean two things that could never be counted together. DIRECTED where the upstream says so: dict-sme-nob and dict-nob-sme are separately published and a dictionary that goes one way is a different resource from one that goes the other.

Subject: language
Name: Covered by
Description: OURS: a source that asserts at least one fact about this language. Computed by the projector over the value set for a language, not stored as a value -- so it has no source and cannot be produced by an ingester.

Subject: language
Name: Source count
Description: OURS: how many distinct sources assert a fact about this language. Computed by the projector over the value set for a language, not stored as a value -- so it has no source and cannot be produced by an ingester.

Subject: language
Name: Components present
Description: OURS: how many card components carry a value. Computed by the projector over the value set for a language, not stored as a value -- so it has no source and cannot be produced by an ingester.

Subject: language
Name: Components total
Description: OURS: how many card components exist to be filled. Computed by the projector over the value set for a language, not stored as a value -- so it has no source and cannot be produced by an ingester.

Subject: language
Name: Method support
Description: Whether a translation method covers this language. Existence and capability, never a measured score (lint R3). Variant names the method.

Subject: language
Name: Wikipedia edition
Description: An open Wikipedia edition in this language, with its site code and URL. EXISTENCE ONLY: for many low-resource languages this is the largest body of monolingual running text that exists, and it is not evidence of quality or size. Article counts are deliberately not carried -- several editions are largely bot-generated, and a 200,000-article edition is not 'better documented' than a 2,000-article one in any sense a translator can use.

Subject: language
Name: Superseded ISO code
Description: A retired ISO 639-3 code that SIL now directs to this language. Recorded on the SUCCESSOR because a retired code has no card of its own — published corpora do not update when a registry changes its mind, so a practitioner arriving with the old code needs to find where it went.

Subject: language
Name: Metric model support
Description: An evaluation metric model that publishes coverage of this language, and the model identifier a harness loads. Existence and capability, never a score (lint R3). Variant names the model. AfriCOMET evaluates African languages better than default COMET, so this drives a real choice; the previous source cited the wrong paper on all 109 cards it touched.

Subject: language
Name: Code alias
Description: Another code that resolves to this language. DERIVED from SIL's own ISO 639-1 column: a language holding Part1 'fr' is what 'fr' means. This is what lets a caller type a two-letter code and reach a card, and losing it broke every consumer that does. AMBIGUOUS codes are NOT here -- routing 'zh' to Mandarin is an editorial choice recorded in shared/catalogue/code-routing.json, because it is our decision and not something SIL says.

Subject: language
Name: Politeness distinction
Description: Whether the language grammaticalises politeness in second-person forms. ATTRIBUTED across Grambank GB415 (binary: absent/present) and WALS 45A (four levels: no distinction / binary / multiple / pronouns avoided), which are different scales and are reported as incommensurable rather than as a disagreement. This is the FACT behind what the previous corpus stored as `formality` prose on 1,781 cards and `registers` prompts on 1,775 -- 94% of both were generated from these two sources and then carried as though they were configuration.

Subject: language
Name: Plural categories
Description: The cardinal plural categories this language distinguishes, as CLDR states them -- Arabic has six (zero, one, two, few, many, other), French three, Chinese one. An i18n pipeline needs this to know how many plural forms a message must supply; getting it wrong produces translations that are grammatically impossible rather than merely awkward. Read from the keys of CLDR's own rule set, so it is CLDR's claim and not our derivation.

Subject: language
Name: Canonicalised member
Description: For a MACROLANGUAGE, an individual language whose tag the BCP 47 world folds INTO this macrolanguage's tag. CLDR's alias table (reason=macrolanguage) and SIL's langtags (iso639_3extra) each assert it independently -- Unicode folds for locale identifiers, the langtags editors fold for tag equivalence. Stated as the raw relation and NOT as "the predominant member", because those are not the same claim: `zho` takes exactly one (cmn) and naming it predominant is sound, while `aka` takes two (fat and twi) and Akan simply has no single dominant member. Whether a macrolanguage HAS a predominant member is therefore derived at resolution time from how many members fold in and whether the two registries agree -- one member, both registries, no disagreement, or it is ambiguous. A macrolanguage neither registry folds has none at all, which is why `nor` stays an editorial decision instead of being laundered into a cited one.

Subject: language
Name: BCP 47 tag
Description: The canonical BCP 47 language tag for this language -- what the localisation world calls it, as against what ISO 639-3 calls it. Mandarin is `cmn` here and `zh` there, and both are correct in their own register. Recording it is what lets the atlas speak to Google, DeepL and CLDR without either side's identifier being treated as the only real one.

Subject: language
Name: BCP 47 full tag
Description: The maximal form of the tag -- language, script and region, as in `zh-Hans-CN` or `crk-Cans-CA`. SIL's langtags states it per equivalence set and CLDR's likelySubtags derives it independently. Useful precisely where a bare language code is not enough: it is the difference between asking for Plains Cree and asking for Plains Cree in syllabics.

Subject: language
Name: Suppress script
Description: The script subtag that is REDUNDANT for this language because it is overwhelmingly the only one used -- `Latn` for English, `Cyrl` for Russian. IANA's own registry field, and one of the few things in that registry that is not an echo of ISO 639-3. It tells a tag normaliser when to drop a script rather than when to add one.

Subject: method
Name: Method language count
Description: How many languages a method's OWN published list contains, counted by us from the fetched list. The publisher's claim is a separate thing: a method may advertise a number and publish no enumeration, and the gap between the two is the most informative fact about it. This is the counted one, so it is champollion-derived and never the vendor's assertion.

Subject: method
Name: Method pair count
Description: How many language PAIRS a method publishes, where it publishes pairs at all. LibreTranslate gives every language a `targets` array and Apertium is rule-based and lists pairs outright; most vendors publish only a language list, and for those this is absent rather than computed. Coverage of a language never implies a pair exists, which is why the two counts are separate parameters.

Subject: method
Name: Method pairs observed
Description: Whether the pair set was READ from the publisher or merely assumed from anyToAny. The register asserts anyToAny by hand for eleven methods; for the two that publish pairs it is now observed, and the difference between an observation and an assumption belongs on the card.

Subject: method
Name: Method derived from
Description: The model a method's own card cites as its base. DECLARED ONLY, never inferred: 5,391 HuggingFace models name a base_model, while roughly 6,160 more are plainly re-hosts or format conversions that say nothing — WindstormLabs publishes 3,139 models named `origin-Helsinki-NLP-opus-mt-*`. Reading derivation off a repository name would be manufacturing, because a name is not a citation. The consequence is that a method count is a count of UPLOADS unless it says otherwise, and this field is what lets a reader tell the difference.

Subject: language
Name: FST resource
Description: A finite-state morphological analyser published for this language, with its repository, licence and archived state. EXISTENCE ONLY (boundary invariant kind 2): that an analyser repository exists and who publishes it, never that it compiles, covers the grammar, or is accurate — those are measured claims and belong to a run, not a card. The LICENCE travels with each entry rather than being assumed uniform across the catalogue, because this project's own boundary forbids bundling GPL/AGPL FST code into proprietary CLI paths and that decision needs the actual terms. For a polysynthetic language an FST is frequently the only structural check that exists at all.

Subject: corpus
Name: Corpus pair count
Description: How many language PAIRS a parallel corpus publishes, counted by us from the fetched index. A corpus is not covered by a language count: GlobalVoices names 49 languages and publishes 854 pairs, and which pairs exist is the question a translator actually has.

Subject: corpus
Name: Corpus language count
Description: How many distinct languages appear on either side of a corpus's pairs, counted from the fetched index.

Subject: corpus
Name: Corpus alignment pairs
Description: Total aligned segments across every pair in the corpus, as the publisher's own index reports them. This is the number that decides whether a corpus can resolve anything: median corpus size across our existing cards is 137 segments, and 137 segments cannot distinguish systems differing by less than roughly four chrF++.

Subject: language
Name: Corpus resource
Description: A parallel corpus that attests this language, with the pair it appears in and the publisher's own alignment and token counts. EXISTENCE and SIZE, never quality: that data exists and how much of it, never that it is clean, in-domain, or usable. The pair rides on the value because a corpus attests a language only THROUGH a pair — there is no such thing as monolingual coverage in a parallel corpus, and a card that said 'GlobalVoices covers Swahili' without saying against what would be answering a question nobody asked.

Subject: language
Name: Keyboard layout resource
Description: A published keyboard layout for this language. Existence only. This matters more than its plainness suggests: for a language whose orthography needs characters no standard layout produces, a keyboard layout is the difference between the language being typable at all and not, and it is a prerequisite for every other resource being created by its own speakers.

Subject: language
Name: Monolingual corpus resource
Description: A published monolingual corpus for this language — text in the language, not aligned to another. Kept separate from corpusResource, which is parallel: the two answer different questions, and one shape holding both would make 'has a corpus' mean two incomparable things. Existence only, never size or cleanliness.

Subject: language
Name: Speech resource
Description: A published speech resource for this language. Existence only.

Subject: language
Name: Typological dataset coverage
Description: A typological or structural dataset that CODES this language, with how many features it codes. EXISTENCE AND EXTENT, never content: that uratyp codes Erzya on 360 features is a fact about documentation coverage; what any feature says stays out until a person writes the parameter map that accepts it. This is the same lane Wordlists already use for lexical existence — a StructureDataset with no map is attested, not interpreted, because auto-ingesting semantics under guessed mappings is how a card comes to claim things nobody decided. The feature count is OUR arithmetic over the publisher's rows, so it carries champollion-derived provenance with Derived_From naming the release.

Subject: language
Name: Inclusive/exclusive distinction
Description: Whether independent pronouns distinguish inclusive from exclusive first-person plural. Grambank codes this BINARY (GB028); WALS 39A codes five types — separate Source_Scales, so a card showing both reports them incommensurable rather than disagreeing.

Subject: language
Name: CLICS unique forms
Description: OURS: count of distinct forms attested for this language across CLICS3's aggregated datasets. The denominator of colexificationDensity.

Subject: language
Name: CLICS contributing datasets
Description: OURS: how many of CLICS3's aggregated source datasets attest this language.

Subject: language
Name: Colexification density
Description: OURS: distinct concepts divided by distinct forms, the legacy panel's ratio — above 1.0 means multiple concepts share forms (high colexification). Same arithmetic as the retired ingest so the public panel's number keeps its meaning.

Subject: language
Name: Treebank resource
Description: A published syntactic treebank for this language (Universal Dependencies). EXISTENCE AND EXTENT only — treebank name, sentence/token counts as published, release — never corpus content; the corpus-content quarantine holds here the same as everywhere. One parameter for every treebank with the treebank in Variant, the lexicalResource pattern.

Subject: language
Name: Orthographic status
Description: OURS: a positive-evidence synthesis of in-store signals — CLDR official status (standardized / de-facto-standard), script + CLDR presence or keyboard (has-orthography), script alone (developing). NEVER 'unwritten': the retired parameter asserted it about 1,318 languages because we had failed to harvest a script, and script absence stays absence. Derived only where a signal exists; silence stays silence.

Subject: language
Name: CLICS total entries
Description: OURS: total form entries for this language across CLICS3's aggregated datasets (rows, not distinct forms).

Subject: language
Name: Typology feature catalog
Description: The FULL feature set of a typological catalog (WALS, Grambank, APiCS): one value per language and feature, the upstream feature id as a `feature` variant, the value stated in the publisher's own code label. STORE-ONLY: never projected onto a card and never part of the emitted card-fact dataset — the mapped parameters above are the card-worthy decisions, and this catalog is everything else the source coded, kept attributed and citable for the public catalogue's typology panel. One parameter rather than ~900 near-identical ones, for the same reason lexicalResource is one parameter rather than 145.
